text:
k8s-alert-bot: ALERT: Suspicious image entrypoint change detected. Pod=redwood-worker-3 ns=prod node=node-42 image=redwood/runtime:v2.1 expected_entrypoint=/usr/local/bin/worker found_entrypoint=/bin/sh -c "/usr/bin/wrapper" sha256 mismatch: expected=abc123... found=deadbeef...
Alex (oncall): seen it, ack. pulling node-42 out of rotation now.
Alex (oncall): `kubectl cordon node/node-42` and `kubectl drain node/node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` in progress.
Sanjay (eng-runtime): good. please do not delete the node yet — we need disk snapshot and container filesystem. also capture `crictl ps -a` and `crictl inspect <container>` outputs.
Taylor (eng-security): tagging this P1. collect `/var/log/pods/*` and kubelet logs, and preserve `/var/log/containers/*`. don't restart the kubelet.
Jamie (eng-sre): quick check — was this image signed? run `cosign verify docker.io/redwood/runtime:v2.1` and compare digests to registry.
Eve-scan-bot: scan result: image redwood/runtime:v2.1 not signed by cosign, vuln scan shows no critical CVEs but runtime binary differs from baseline (size and entrypoint).
Maria (incident-lead): action items: containment (cordon/drain ✅), evidence collection (disk snapshots, image tar), triage (who had write access to registry), and comms (legal + CISO). Alex, assign SRE for snapshot. Ravi, start forensic collection.
Ravi (forensics): starting live collection. command to save filesystem: `crictl image pull` then `crictl image save` and `tar -cvf /tmp/node-42-containerfs.tar /var/lib/kubelet/pods/<podid>/volumes`. also collecting `journalctl -u kubelet` and `dmesg`.
Priya (infra): creating a GCP snapshot of node-42 now. ETA ~12m.
Taylor (eng-security): we need to check RBAC/service-account exposure. run `kubectl -n prod get pods -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.spec.serviceAccountName}
{end}'` then `kubectl describe sa <sa> -n prod` — any high-privilege clusterrolebindings?
Sanjay (eng-runtime): also check image pull secrets: `kubectl -n prod get secrets | grep reg` and verify which secrets are mounted into the compromised pod. If registry creds are exposed rotate them immediately.
Jamie (eng-sre): confirm registry activity: `gcr.io audit logs` show push from CI service account at 2026-03-18T02:17:03Z, tag v2.1 pushed by circleci-bot@redwood with digest abc123... but node digest is deadbeef... suspicious.
Maria (incident-lead): Nick (legal), heads up: possible image tamper and potential data exposure — need timeline and customer impact assessment.
Nick (legal): acknowledged. what accounts/tokens might have been available to that pod? also advise holding any external disclosure until we have initial triage.
Alex (oncall): rotating KMS keys for secrets used by prod cluster? we should rotate registry key and any KMS keys that service accounts had access to. This might be heavy-handed but safer.
Taylor (eng-security): agree: rotate registry creds and revoke tokens for the CI service account until we validate pipeline integrity. also rotate KMS DEKs that are used to decrypt S3 buckets if pod mounted volumes had keys. document required KMS key ARNs.
Sanjay (eng-runtime): we need to confirm whether the image on the node was replaced locally or pulled modified. check `/var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.content.v1.content/` for blob entries and compare timestamps.
Eve-scan-bot: Note: recent kubelet upgrade completed on node-42 2026-03-15 — check if node was compromised via kubelet or host path mounts.
Ravi (forensics): capturing network connections from the container: `ss -tunap` and docker/netstat outputs. collecting outbound connections during compromise window.
Priya (infra): registry creds rotation started. Blocking all pulls from node-42 IP at edge ACLs.
Maria (incident-lead): communications: prepare internal post-incident channel #sec-incident-1802504444 and incident doc. Do not post public notice yet.
Jamie (eng-sre): quick mitigation: add an admission webhook to block images without verified signatures (cosign) for prod. can we toggle in fail-open? prefer fail-closed for prod until we finish triage.
Taylor (eng-security): enable apiserver audit logging (policy to record ImagePullSecrets, Pod execs, Exec, and Node-level events) and increase retention for the last 90 days.
Alex (oncall): we found evidence that the /bin/sh wrapper was added after container start — implies local modification. looking into host-level compromise vector.
Sanjay (eng-runtime): check for any containers running with hostPID or hostMounts; `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o yaml | grep hostPath` — scanning cluster for hostPath usage.
Ravi (forensics): pulled containerfs tar and checksums. baseline binary sha256=7f8e... current binary sha256=1a2b... storing artifacts in secure bucket `gs://redwood-incidents/1802504444/` with kms key `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/incidents/cryptoKeys/1802-key` (we will rotate after snapshot).
Nick (legal): we need chain-of-custody notes for all artifacts. ensure logs show who accessed the incident bucket.
Maria (incident-lead): next steps: 1) complete forensics and confirm scope, 2) rotate credentials/keys, 3) block affected images and nodes, 4) schedule postmortem and timeline, 5) review CI pipeline and cosign signing. assign owners and ETA 24h.
Taylor (eng-security): follow-up: audit who has write access to the registry and CI signing keys, update RBAC to enforce least-privilege, and set up automated cosign verification in CI.
Alex (oncall): final note: all deploying teams paused prod deployments for the next 4 hours. will update when we have digest origin confirmed. :warning:
Maria (incident-lead): recording this as incident #INC-2026-03018. creating calendar for incident review + legal review.
Ravi (forensics): last collection done at 1802506310. storing artifact manifest in incident doc.
Alex (oncall): thanks team. keep posts short and actionable in the incident channel.
